To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HE source IGR J17457-2901 is a compact but diffuse region of non-thermal X-ray emission located ~1' from Sgr A*. Its HE spectrum is well described by a power-law of photon index 1.8 and its luminosity is 5.4x 10^35 erg/s at a distance of 8 kpc.

the HE spectrum of the central region of the Galaxy is a power law with a photon index of 2.1+/-0.1 and that the HE emission from the GC region is dominated by the non-thermal emission from the compact diffuse region located within a few arcmins of Sgr A*, with a 20-400keV luminosity of 5.4x1035 erg/sec.

the HE source IGR J17454-2901 is persistent and is located at R.A.=17:45:42.5 and decl.=-28:59:28'' with 1'' accuracy, that its spectrum is hard, and that the HE emission from this region is most likely diffuse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of a new HE component in the central arcmins region of the GC, which we believe is a compact, diffuse, non-thermally-emitting region.
a persistent, compact, non-thermal HE g-ray source located within 1 arcmin of the central BH of the Galaxy and with an HE spectrum extending up to at least 400 keV.
the study of the central parsecs of the Milky Way, which is the only region of the Galaxy where the BH is known to be active.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HE emission from the GC is a complex mixture of contributions from a number of different physical processes, some of which are still unknown.
the GC is a persistent HE g-ray source.

the HE emission region is located within a few arcseconds of Sgr A*, and that it is likely to be a compact non-thermal region of diffuse HE g-ray emission, with the SgrA East SNR as a potential contributor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have detected for the first-time the emission of the central arcmins region of the Galaxy in the HE band.
we have detected and studied a HE source, IGR, located within 2" of the central black hole of our Galaxy, Sgr A*, and that we have constructed the first accurate wide-band spectrum of the GC region.
, in addition to the radio and infrared sources, there is a compact, non-thermal HE source in the vicinity of Sgr A*, which could be a counterpart of the ~TeV g-ray source recently detected by Hess.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the central parsec of our Galaxy harbours a persistent, compact, and diffuse source of HE emission.
the GC region harbors a compact, diffuse source of HE emission which is likely to be associated with the BH and its environment.
the central arcmins around Sgr A* are a very active region in the GC and that it should be the focus of future HE and very HE observations.
